title: Short Stuff: The Bell Witch
summary: Josh and Chuck cover the Bell Witch legend of Adams, Tennessee, a supposed poltergeist haunting of the Bell family beginning in 1817. The episode covers the first sightings (a dog-rabbit creature, a giant bird, a green-dressed girl), nightly pounding and physical attacks, the witch's speaking voice, the enslaved man Dean's encounters and the witch ball, Betsy Bell's engagement to Joshua Gardner and her later marriage, John Bell's illness and death in December 1820 which the witch claimed to have caused by poison, the 1849 Saturday Evening Post story and Betsy's threatened lawsuit, and the rival explanations involving Kate Batts (land deal with Benjamin Batts, or an affair and a smokehouse death). It closes with tourism at the replica house and cave near Adams.

segments.title: Opening and setup
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck introduce the Short Stuff on the Bell Witch, set the scene in Adams, Tennessee, and note the sources, including historian Pat Fitzhugh's book and website.

segments.title: First sightings
segments.summary: In 1817 John Bell shoots at a dog-headed rabbit creature in his field. His son Drury sees a giant bird on a fence post, and daughter Betsy reports a green-dressed girl hanging from a tree.

segments.title: Nightly pounding and early disturbances
segments.summary: Pounding on the walls starts the same night and continues nightly, with the family searching in vain. Children hear rats chewing bedposts.

segments.title: Physical attacks and the talking voice
segments.summary: The hauntings become physical, with sheets pulled off, Betsy slapped, pinched and hair-pulled. The witch's voice grows clearer and holds conversations; John Bell Jr. later wrote them down and published them in 1934.

segments.title: Dean the enslaved man and the witch ball
segments.summary: The enslaved man Dean encounters a two-headed dog. His wife made him a witch ball, a blown glass sphere used to trap or ward off witches.

segments.title: Ad break
segments.summary: Break before the second half of the episode.

segments.title: Betsy's engagement and John Bell's illness
segments.summary: The witch opposed Betsy's engagement to Joshua Gardner, and she married an old man she nursed for eleven years. John Bell fell ill after the witch appeared and was slapped around during his seizures.

segments.title: John Bell's death and local legends
segments.summary: John Bell died in December 1820, believing the witch poisoned him, which she reportedly confirmed. Neighbors tried to catch the witch and local legends arose, including the witch reciting two sermons at once.

segments.title: Funeral and 1849 Saturday Evening Post article
segments.summary: The witch reportedly interrupted John Bell's funeral. In 1849 the Saturday Evening Post published a story blaming Betsy, who threatened to sue and got an apology and retraction.

segments.title: Kate Batts explanations
segments.summary: The witch was attributed to local woman Kate Batts. One explanation is a land deal in which John Bell took advantage of her brother-in-law Benjamin Batts; the other is an affair and Bell leaving her tied in a smokehouse to die.

segments.title: Real people and historical record
segments.summary: Genealogists have found Kate Batts in Edgecombe County and in Adams, Tennessee, and the Bell family graveyard holds headstones from the period, making the legend feel real.

segments.title: Tourism at Adams, Tennessee
segments.summary: Adams has a replica of the Bell house and a cave on John Bell's property, both open to tour, including lantern-guided tours. Chuck jokes about an animatronic rabbit dog.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck close the episode and mention iHeartRadio.
